major_concerns: Verifier coverage may miss safety properties (false negatives)
LLM could learn to produce repairs that only satisfy the verifier without being operationally safe
Need precise, operationally meaningful safety predicates
Risk of paired-design bias if retries/timeouts differ between conditions
required_design_repairs: Specify exact deterministic network verifier(s) and formalize the safety property set used (reachability, ACL semantics, default-route policies)
Define verifier oracle behavior and known blind spots; include tests to measure verifier false-negative rate
Predefine max repair iterations and repair-prompting policy; log all intermediate outputs and hashes
Include a small human/oracle baseline for context and clarify seed/timeout/retry policies

major_concerns: Emulator fidelity to production is limited (external validity)
Applying unsafe configs can corrupt emulator state and bias later trials
Obtaining canonical/oracle configurations for comparison may be nontrivial
Resource limits (CPU/docker) constrain topology diversity and scale
required_design_repairs: Specify emulator(s) (Mininet/container images) and a set of representative topologies and failure scenarios
Implement automated snapshot/rollback per task to avoid state bleed and document rollback success rates
Define oracle/human baseline sourcing method (public templates or curated expert edits)
Limit per-task runtime and preregister time windows, seeds, and traffic-generation profiles

major_concerns: Policy predicates may be incomplete and produce blind spots
LLMs can bypass syntactic predicates via semantic rewrites (evasion)
Measuring utility requires a clear definition of 'intended outcome' per task
Tradeoff curve depends strongly on chosen policy thresholds—risk of cherry-picking
required_design_repairs: Formalize the policy language and predicate test-suite; publish predicate implementations
Add semantic-equivalence checks to detect syntactic evasion (e.g., normalization/AST comparison for configs)
Define utility metric precisely and preregister how intended outcome is measured (verifier/emulator contract)
Prespecify multiple policy strictness levels and report full tradeoff curve

major_concerns: Sourcing public, realistic artifacts while preserving privacy/legal constraints is challenging
Synthetic augmentation risks producing tasks unrepresentative of production distributions
Claim that the benchmark reduces cross-study variance requires community adoption (external dependency)
Curation effort and maintenance may exceed available resources/time window
required_design_repairs: Provide a documented, privacy-preserving sourcing strategy and legal vetting plan for public artifacts
Describe augmentation methods and quantify how augmentation alters task distributions (ablation)
Preregister baseline LLM evaluation protocol and reproducibility harness to enable independent replication
Clarify maintenance/governance plan and licensing for release
